Par_Projektu_Apr: Baltic Shorts is a streaming platform focused on showcasing short films by Baltic filmmakers. We aim to create and maintain an easy-to-use catalogue of a wide range of films that strengthens the accessibility of the short film form and the visibility of its creators.
about_apraksts_1: BalticShorts.com is a unique streaming platform dedicated to solving an issue for both emerging and well-established filmmakers from the Baltic region: the lack of accessible, artist and audience-focused spaces that align with their values and can showcase their short film projects. Even more, for artists who are just starting out, visibility is essential for growth. Film school students create innovative short films every year, yet these works often remain unseen by a larger public.
about_apraksts_2: As filmmakers ourselves, we recognize the challenges of gaining exposure from works that aren’t meant to entertain the masses. BalticShorts.com is a solution to this problem, designed to provide a dedicated space for these works to reach broader audiences, both regionally and internationally.
about_apraksts_3: Our platform is the only Baltic creator-focused VOD service solely dedicated to short films. It offers a curated catalogue of high-quality works sourced directly from regional film schools as well as through open submissions.
about_apraksts_4: Each film featured on BalticShorts.com is treated as a collaborative effort - showcasing not only the director but the entire production team, including cinematographers, production designers, actors, and other essential contributors. By highlighting these roles, BalticShorts.com functions as both a streaming platform and a professional portfolio for filmmakers, helping them connect with audiences and industry professionals alike.
about_apraksts_5: Made by filmmakers for filmmakers, BalticShorts.com is commited to supporting emerging talent, fostering new connections, and celebrating the distinct voices of Baltic cinema. We aim to create a sustainable and supportive environment where Baltic short films can find the audience they deserve.
